images.text: For more than 1,500 years, the city of Pompeii lay almost entirely buried under volcanic ash and pumice. The mighty Mount Vesuvius had erupted spewing tons of sooty ash. Citizens who had the ability to do so, fled on boats to safety when they realized the severity of the situation and the potency of the volcano. This dramatic event, horrific for the inhabitants, has given us a fantastic legacy.</br></br>Much information about the domestic, artistic and athletic lives of the people who lived in this city which had a complex water system, an amphitheatre, gymnasium, and a port is known in great detail. The incredible discovery and careful reconstruction of Pompeii has provided valuable information on life in an Italian city 2,000 years ago.

At the time of the eruption, Pompeii had reached its high point in society as many Romans frequently visited Pompeii on vacations. It is the only ancient town where the whole topographic structure is known precisely as it was, with no later modifications or additions.</br></br>Excavations have revealed that few valuable objects were left behind in Pompeii. Archaeologists believe that people took their valuable items with them and also came back later to look for things. People even removed some of the marble on the buildings!

However, it's a fallacy to think that all of the people in Pompeii escaped. Many did not. They were covered, along with the city, in the wet ash that engulfed it. The ash dried, then hardened, sealing everything in. Their bodies disintegrated over time, leaving empty molds.</br></br>From these, archeologists were able to create amazing true-to-life statues of Pompeians in the privacy of their last moments. Some of them can be viewed, frozen in time forever, in the museum at Pompeii.

Linking is very common in natural conversation. Linking happens when certain sounds are connected. This happens between function words (like articles or prepositions) and content words (like nouns or verbs). It also happens particularly when there is a consonant at the end of one word and a vowel at the beginning of the next.

Get out ...
You pronounce this as: get_out (getaut)

This linking pattern not only joins two words, but can also link three or more words together.

For example:

Have an egg ...
You pronounce this as: have_an_egg (havenegg)

Stress with Suffixes: One and Two Syllables Before the Suffix

When you look at words in reverse, from the end of the word toward the front, a pattern of stress starts to appear.   </br></br>These patterns can help you become familiar with how certain words are pronounced.

For instance, the words classic, specific, and economic all include the -ic suffix. They are stressed on the first, second, and third syllables, respectively. The stress patterns can only be found when it is understood that syllables must be counted from the end of the word toward the beginning of the word.

Let's look at the words classic, specific and economic. They all end in the suffix -ic. When you read them aloud, they do not necessarily follow a pattern. But, try looking at the them in reverse. You will notice a pattern.

Other suffixes have different rules. When you look at words with the suffixes -ity and -acy, you will notice a slightly different pattern. Look at the chart to see this pattern. The bolded syllables are stressed.
